rationale: The candidate reads as a compact stepped/cantilevered mass, but the four views do not converge on one strong spatial rule. The object is coherent enough in silhouette, yet the stacked/fractured upper pieces feel more like a clipped or over-edited extrusion than a clearly inhabited neighborhood building. Most importantly, the verified frontage edge is answered weakly: the blue access line is adjacent to the mass, but the ground condition stays mostly sealed, with no convincing public court, notch, undercut, or entry seam opening toward the access side. The visible void is too shallow to carry the program’s required active threshold and public-space logic. The mass also leans toward a generic stepped object rather than a neighborhood living figure with a legible public ground and calm upper hierarchy. Reference 1 supports a courtyard/terrace principle; reference 2 supports a simple public edge and setback; reference 3 suggests a stronger sectional/terraced continuity, but it is not directly transferable as-is.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Larger campus-like spread and multiple wings; candidate is much more compact and the open-space logic is weaker.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard-linked neighborhood massing with terraced connectors and a clear communal void sequence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Single-story pavilion typology is not a direct match to the candidate’s multi-level compact mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Small street-facing public volume with a simple, legible canopy/entry setback and active ground edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual reference is larger and more explicitly sectional; candidate lacks the same quality of continuous inhabited section.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/sectional massing can support neighborhood living when the void and ground relation stay legible.

warnings: Parcel containment appears to pass visually, but containment alone is not enough here.
Solids do not visibly collide across views, but the mass reads as over-fractured and semantically weak at ground level.
The access edge response is semantically opposite to the brief: the street edge is present but not actively opened.
No hard program-section requirement is present, so failure is due to program fit and threshold logic rather than roof type alone.
